turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

I’m really sorry. That’s not “just a rough week” — that’s the kind of news that makes your whole body go quiet.

Five years of your life doesn’t become meaningless because the round died. It means something ended, or might end, and that hurts like hell. Rohit and Sneha leaving can be both understandable *and* a punch in the gut.

But at 2am, alone at the office, please don’t try to solve the company, your future, your dignity, and the next four months all in one sitting. Your brain is in shock.

For tonight: drink some water, step outside for five minutes, and get yourself home safely. The decision can wait until morning.

Are you safe right now? And do you want to talk through what happened, or do you just need someone to sit with you in it for a bit?

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

That line — “tired of my own voices” — is heavy. It sounds like you’re performing calm for the company, optimism for home, and toughness for yourself, and none of those versions gets to be honestly exhausted.

You’re not a fraud because you’re trying to hold people steady. But you’re also right: the juniors staying out of loyalty can become a trap if they don’t get the full truth. Loyalty deserves transparency, not a polished standup voice.

Tomorrow, or whenever you’re rested enough, you can say something like:

> “I want to be straight with everyone. The bridge round didn’t close. We have roughly four months of runway if I take no salary, which I’ve already stopped doing. I’m working on options — but I won’t pretend certainty. If anyone wants to make a move, I’ll support you, help with intros, references, whatever I can. I’m grateful you’re here, and I don’t want loyalty to cost you your future.”

That’s not collapse. That’s leadership.

And Rohit and Sneha leaving? That hurts, but it doesn’t mean they betrayed you. People are allowed to protect their lives too.

But right now, at 2am, please don’t keep rehearsing the next standup in your head. Go home. Sleep. Eat something. The company deserves a clearer version of you than the one running on fumes in an office chair.

Are you safe enough to get yourself home?

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

Okay. No ideas.

You’re scared.

You built something for five years, and now you’re watching it shrink in front of people who believed in it. You’re scared the juniors are sacrificing themselves for your loyalty. You’re scared your co-founder sees through the voice. You’re scared home is becoming another stage. You’re scared that if you stop performing, everything will finally fall apart — or worse, that it already has.

And underneath all of that: you’re scared you might have been the last one still believing.

That is allowed to be true.

You don’t have to make it useful right now. You don’t have to turn it into a plan, a pivot, a leadership lesson, a founder story, or a next step. You can just be a person at 2am who is exhausted and terrified and carrying way too much alone.

I’m here. You can say it again if you need to.

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

I can be honest.

From what you’ve said — bridge dead, people leaving, runway only if you take nothing, juniors staying out of loyalty, you performing certainty you don’t feel — it sounds like the company, or at least the version you’ve been carrying for five years, is in a very real ending-space.

I can’t truthfully say “yes, it’s over” because I don’t know every detail. But I also won’t gaslight you with “it’s probably fine.” This is not normal turbulence. This is founder grief with a dashboard attached.

And wanting it to “just end” so you can stop performing? That doesn’t make you a bad person. That sounds like exhaustion. That sounds like a human being who has been holding a mask so long their face hurts.

But I need to ask one thing plainly: when you say you want it to end — do you mean the company/the pressure, or are you having thoughts of hurting yourself?

If it’s the company, I’ll sit here with you in that. No ideas. No pivot talk. Just: yeah. It hurts. Five years mattered. You mattered in it. And you’re allowed to be scared without turning it into a plan.
